subject: Horizon.ai commit planning — mixed workload TPS & latency headroom
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Soto <m.soto@horizon.ai>, Ops Team <ops@horizon.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Horizon.ai commit planning — mixed workload TPS & latency headroom

Hi Maya / Horizon Ops,

Kicking off the dedicated sizing discussion so we can align on a committed capacity that meets your real-time chat SLOs plus the nightly embedding batch. High level notes up front:

- You indicated a steady-state of ~1.2M tokens/day across two primary traffic patterns: interactive chats (40% of tokens, spiky) and embeddings (60%, batch).
- Target SLOs you mentioned: p50 < 120ms for chat generation, p95 < 480ms; batch embeddings can be background with p95 < 60s.
- Your pilot uses an Llama-2-70B variant with 8k context; you requested a single-region (us-west) Dedicated pool with canary fallback to a quantized variant for extreme spikes.

Requesting the following from your side so we can finalize our sizing model:
1) Typical chat request length (prompt+expected completion) in tokens for the top 3 user flows.
2) Expected concurrency during peak 10-minute windows (approx).
3) Any hard latency blackouts (e.g., synchronous payments flows that must not exceed 200ms).

I'll attach a first-pass capacity model (xlsx) with tokens/sec maps and GPU-sku assumptions. Laura / Ben — looping you in for SLO-fit and slab recommendations.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_model_horizon_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Maya Soto <m.soto@horizon.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@horizon.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Horizon.ai commit planning — mixed workload TPS & latency headroom

Thanks Rishi — quick answers inline: 

- Top chat flows average 85 tokens (flow A), 140 tokens (flow B), and 360 tokens for long-form (flow C). Completions average ~60 tokens.
- Peak concurrency: about 520 concurrent chat sessions in the US-west at typical peak (10-min rolling), but spikes to ~1,100 for 3–5 minutes during product launches.
- No hard 200ms blackouts; payments are out-of-band. Primary concern is keeping p95 < 500ms for interactive flows.

We reviewed your attached sheet and have one ask: can you size for a conservative 30% traffic growth over the next 12 months and show a cost/latency tradeoff if we accept an H100 quantized fallback for p95 during extreme spikes?

Maya
Head of Cloud Ops, Horizon.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Soto <m.soto@horizon.ai>, Ops Team <ops@horizon.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Sep 2028 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Horizon.ai commit planning — mixed workload TPS & latency headroom

Maya — thanks, that helps a lot.

Summary of our first-pass sizing (attached workbook contains the full math):

- Workload mix: chat (40%) | embeddings (60%) based on your traffic profile and token averages.
- Modeled peak 10-min window after +30% growth: 1,430 concurrent chat sessions -> estimated chat qps (requests) ~24 req/s assuming mean think time; token/sec demand for chat generation: ~68k tokens/sec at peak burst (includes both prompt and completion).
- Embedding batch throughput: ~1.2M sentence embeddings overnight; modeled as a background job with sustained 900 tokens/sec equivalent during the 02:00–06:00 window.

GPU slab recommendations (tradeoffs):
1) Minimal SLA fit (cost-min): 6 x H100-80GB quantized pool (serve quantized 70B) — expected p95 chat = ~520–760ms (uses higher batching, minimal KV warm-up). Risk: p95 occasionally above target during multi-minute launches.
2) Balanced (recommended): 10 x H100-80GB mixed pool with 4 GPUs reserved for low-latency hot-path (non-quantized) and 6 GPUs for bulk quantized capacity; expected p95 chat = ~320–420ms with 30% headroom for short spikes.
3) Aggressive SLO (low latency): 14 x H100-80GB hot-path heavy configuration (more non-quantized instances, prewarmed KV shards) — expected p95 chat < 240ms consistently, higher monthly commit.

Key modeling assumptions (please review):
- Model: llama-2-70b (fp16 baseline) / int4 quantized variant latency reductions approximate 2.3x token/sec improvement per GPU under continuous batching.
- KV cache warm state reduces cold-start token cost by ~45% after a 90s warm window in our simulations.
- Network overhead to customer region modeled at 12–18ms median.

Attachments: capacity_model_horizon_v2.xlsx (sheet tabs: summary, peak-scenarios, gpu-sku-math, cost-breakdown), horizon_slo_runbook.pdf

Action items:
- Laura: can you validate the headroom math and suggest bounding slab counts for the Balanced recommendation?
- Ben: please prepare a committed pricing estimate for the Balanced and Aggressive options (monthly committed spend, burst credits, and rollback terms).
- Maya: if Balanced looks acceptable, we can draft a mutual action plan and DocuSign the commitment; I added a HubSpot link below for the deal.

Best,
Rishi

Thanks — I validated the math in the attached workbook and made two small adjustments to the Balanced slab sizing:

- Increased reserved hot-path GPUs from 4 -> 5 to account for KV eviction pressure at 90% utilization.
- Added a 10% buffer on quantized pool capacity for parallel embedding jobs that may sometimes overlap into daytime maintenance windows.

Final Balanced recommendation (updated): 11 x H100-80GB (5 hot-path non-quantized, 6 quantized slab) — estimated p95 chat = 300–380ms under the modeled +30% growth scenario with expected headroom for 3–4 minute launch spikes.

Ben — pricing request outstanding from your side; please include commit term options (12/24/36) and an accelerated delivery clause for capacity bursts.

Maya — if you confirm this Balanced slab, we can generate a mutual action plan and provide a DocuSign for signatures. I included a short runbook section (horizon_slo_runbook.pdf) describing the canary fallback behavior and operational playbook.

Laura
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
